content.json:
# Umbraco Load Test Dashboard
Data sources in the workspace below, populated on every pipeline run:
- `LoadTestSummary_CL` (+ per-minute `LoadTestSeries_CL`) — server-side throughput & capacity, from `scripts/publish-load-test-results.ps1`.
- `ClientMeasurement_CL` — browser-perceived backoffice latency (see the **Client measurements** tab), from `scripts/publish-client-results.ps1`.

Open the **Glossary** tab for the full vocabulary.

parameters.name: Scenario
parameters.label: Scenario
parameters.query:
LoadTestSummary_CL
| distinct scenario
| where isnotempty(scenario)
| order by scenario asc

parameters.name: Version
parameters.label: Version
parameters.query:
LoadTestSummary_CL
| distinct umbraco_version
| where isnotempty(umbraco_version)
| order by parse_version(umbraco_version) asc

parameters.name: Tier
parameters.label: Tier
parameters.query:
LoadTestSummary_CL
| distinct infra_tier
| where isnotempty(infra_tier)
| order by infra_tier asc

content.json: _Filters above scope **Trends**, **Compare**, and **Runs**. **Tiers** and **Versions** have their own pickers; they default to the matching global values when set._

content.query:
// Latest-run summary card. Top-of-page glance answer to 'is the latest
// run OK?' Pulls one row per (scenario × version × tier) bounded by the
// global filter. Capacity status flags infra saturation (Server CPU /
// memory / Database load peaks at 85/95% or error rate at 1%);
// Regression surfaces the verdict posted by scripts/check-regression.ps1
// for the same case.
// publish-load-test-results.ps1 writes one row per sampler with the
// run-level resource metrics (plan_*, sql_*) duplicated across every
// row of the same run. arg_max picks one row per case and its resource
// fields ARE the run-level values — no need to filter to an empty
// scenario_name (which would exclude everything).
let runs = LoadTestSummary_CL
    | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
    | where '{Scenario}' == '*' or scenario == '{Scenario}'
    | where '{Version}' == '*' or umbraco_version == '{Version}'
    | where '{Tier}' == '*' or infra_tier == '{Tier}'
    | where parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
    | extend run_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', tostring(run_id))), scenario_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', scenario)), version_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', umbraco_version)), tier_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', infra_tier))
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by run_key, scenario_key, version_key, tier_key
    | top 5 by TimeGenerated desc;
let regression = LoadTestSummary_CL
    | where parse_status == 'regression_check'
    | extend run_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', tostring(run_id))), scenario_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', scenario)), version_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', umbraco_version)), tier_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', infra_tier))
    | summarize regression_status = take_any(regression_status), reg_ts = max(TimeGenerated) by run_key, scenario_key, version_key, tier_key;
runs
| join kind=leftouter regression on run_key, scenario_key, version_key, tier_key
| extend run_error_rate = todouble(coalesce(error_rate, real(0)))
| extend bn_peak = coalesce(max_of(plan_CpuPercentage_max, plan_MemoryPercentage_max, sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max, sql_cpu_percent_max, sql_log_write_percent_max, sql_physical_data_read_percent_max), real(0))
// Decision-first column order: identifier, verdict triple (Capacity/Bottleneck/
// Regression), then the supporting metric columns.
| project Started = TimeGenerated,
          Scenario = scenario,
          Version = umbraco_version,
          Tier = infra_tier,
          ['Capacity status'] = case(
              run_error_rate >= 0.01
                or plan_CpuPercentage_max >= 95
                or plan_MemoryPercentage_max >= 95
                or sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max >= 95
                or sql_cpu_percent_max >= 95, 'Saturated',
              plan_CpuPercentage_max >= 85
                or plan_MemoryPercentage_max >= 85
                or sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max >= 85
                or sql_cpu_percent_max >= 85, 'Stressed',
              'OK'),
          Bottleneck = case(
              bn_peak < 50, '—',
              plan_CpuPercentage_max == bn_peak, strcat('App CPU ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              plan_MemoryPercentage_max == bn_peak, strcat('Server memory ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max == bn_peak, strcat('Database load ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              sql_cpu_percent_max == bn_peak, strcat('Database CPU ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              sql_log_write_percent_max == bn_peak, strcat('Database log-write ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              sql_physical_data_read_percent_max == bn_peak, strcat('Database physical reads ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              '—'),
          Regression = case(
              regression_status == 'regress',      'regression detected',
              regression_status == 'pass',         'no regression',
              regression_status == 'insufficient', 'not enough history',
              isnotempty(regression_status),       regression_status,
              TimeGenerated > ago(15min),          'checking',
              'not run'),
          ['Error %']          = round(run_error_rate * 100, 2),
          ['Run #'] = run_id,
          ['Server CPU avg %'] = round(plan_CpuPercentage_avg, 1),
          ['Server CPU peak %'] = round(plan_CpuPercentage_max, 1),
          ['Database load avg %']  = round(sql_dtu_consumption_percent_avg, 1),
          ['Database load peak %']  = round(sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max, 1)
| order by Started desc
content.title: Latest 5 runs (chronological) — quick status check on the most recent activity across the global filter. Complements the issues panel above (which is severity-sorted and only shows what's flagged).

content.json:
## Trends
One line per `(sampler × version × tier)` across recent runs. The latest-run card above is the at-a-glance capacity check; the chart below is the longitudinal view, with a foldout matrix showing median ± spread per cell. **Cold-start runs (queued with `skipWarmup: true`) are excluded by default — see the Runs tab to view them, or the Compare tab to pick one explicitly.**

parameters.name: Metric
parameters.label: Metric
parameters.jsonData:
[
    { "value": "p95 (ms)", "label": "p95 (ms)" },
    { "value": "p99 (ms)", "label": "p99 (ms)" },
    { "value": "avg (ms)", "label": "avg (ms)" },
    { "value": "error rate", "label": "error rate" },
    { "value": "Requests/sec", "label": "Requests/sec" },
    { "value": "Server CPU peak %", "label": "Server CPU peak %" },
    { "value": "Database load peak %", "label": "Database load peak %" }
]

parameters.name: Sampler
parameters.label: Sampler

content.title: {Metric} per run — one line per (sampler · version · tier). Ignore the (Sum) totals next to each series in the legend; that's the chart engine summing values across runs, which isn't a meaningful number — read each series line directly.
Resource pressure per run — Server CPU, Server memory, Database load, Database CPU peaks. (Ignore the (Sum) totals in the legend — chart artifact, not meaningful.)

content.query:
// 'error rate' is 0..1 and rounds to '0 ± 0' at integer precision — use 3
// decimals for fractional metrics, integers for everything else. Metric
// translation inlined because KQL column_ifexists requires a literal.
let precision = iif('{Metric}' == 'error rate', 3, 0);
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| where '{Scenario}' == '*' or scenario == '{Scenario}'
| where '{Version}' == '*' or umbraco_version == '{Version}'
| where '{Tier}' == '*' or infra_tier == '{Tier}'
| where '*' in ({Sampler}) or scenario_name in ({Sampler})
| where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| extend value = case(
    '{Metric}' == 'p95 (ms)',              toreal(p95_ms),
    '{Metric}' == 'p99 (ms)',              toreal(p99_ms),
    '{Metric}' == 'avg (ms)',              toreal(avg_ms),
    '{Metric}' == 'error rate',            toreal(error_rate),
    '{Metric}' == 'Requests/sec',          toreal(requests_per_sec),
    '{Metric}' == 'Server CPU peak %',     toreal(plan_CpuPercentage_max),
    '{Metric}' == 'Database load peak %',  toreal(sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max),
    real(null))
| where isnotnull(value)
| summarize med_raw = percentile(value, 50), sd_raw = stdev(value), n = count() by scenario_name, umbraco_version, infra_tier
| extend med = round(med_raw, precision), sd = round(sd_raw, precision)
// Stability is the coefficient of variation (stdev/median × 100) bucketed into
// plain-language labels. Computed from pre-round values so a 3-decimal metric
// like error rate doesn't lose precision to rounding. Thresholds align with the
// default 10% regression-check sensitivity — cells noisier than that need
// wider thresholds before a regression call is meaningful.
| extend cv = iif(n < 5 or med_raw == 0, real(null), sd_raw / med_raw * 100.0)
| extend Stability = case(
    isnull(cv),  'few runs',
    cv < 10,     'stable',
    cv < 25,     'moderate',
                 'noisy')
| project Sampler = scenario_name, Version = umbraco_version, Tier = infra_tier, ['median ± spread (runs)'] = strcat(med, ' ± ', sd, ' (', n, ' runs)'), Stability
| order by Sampler asc, Version asc, Tier asc
content.title: Matrix view — median {Metric} ± spread across runs, plus Stability per cell. Noisy cells mean run-to-run spread is wide enough that a small regression threshold won't be meaningful.

content.json:
## Tiers
Compare tiers for one `(scenario, version)` combination. Answers "what do I get for upgrading the tier?" Pick the scenario and version below; the tables and chart aggregate across every matching run — medians for latency/throughput, plus a worst-case column on each resource peak so a single saturated run still flags Saturated. The **Runs** column shows how many runs back each median; cells with 1 run are single-run snapshots, 3+ runs is statistically meaningful. When the global filter at the top is narrowed, the pickers default to the matching scenario/version automatically. **Cold-start runs are excluded; see the Runs tab for those.**

parameters.name: TiersScenario
parameters.label: Scenario

parameters.name: TiersVersion
parameters.label: Version
parameters.query:
// Show all versions; if the global Version filter is set, sort the matching
// version to the top so showDefault picks it. Otherwise newest-first.
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where scenario == '{TiersScenario}'
| where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| distinct umbraco_version
| where isnotempty(umbraco_version)
| order by iif(umbraco_version == '{Version}', 0, 1) asc, parse_version(umbraco_version) desc

content.query:
// Resource metrics (plan_*, sql_*) and requests_per_sec are duplicated across
// every per-sampler row of the same run by the publish script. Reduce to one
// row per (tier, run_id) first, then aggregate by tier across runs.
//
// Peaks show worst-case (max across runs). Capacity status, Headroom, and
// Bottleneck all derive from worst so a single saturated run flags the tier
// — and the resource columns on the right tell you why.
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where scenario == '{TiersScenario}' and umbraco_version == '{TiersVersion}'
| where parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by infra_tier, run_id
| extend run_error_rate = todouble(coalesce(error_rate, real(0)))
| summarize
    Runs                                = count(),
    ['Requests/sec']                    = round(percentile(todouble(requests_per_sec), 50), 1),
    ['Server CPU avg %']                = round(percentile(plan_CpuPercentage_avg, 50), 1),
    ['Server CPU peak %']               = round(max(plan_CpuPercentage_max), 1),
    ['Server memory peak %']            = round(max(plan_MemoryPercentage_max), 1),
    ['Database load avg %']             = round(percentile(sql_dtu_consumption_percent_avg, 50), 1),
    ['Database load peak %']            = round(max(sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max), 1),
    ['Database CPU peak %']             = round(max(sql_cpu_percent_max), 1),
    ['Database physical reads peak %']  = round(max(sql_physical_data_read_percent_max), 1),
    ['Database log-write peak %']       = round(max(sql_log_write_percent_max), 1),
    ['Error %']                         = round(max(run_error_rate) * 100, 2),
    // Seeder duration (s) — null on Skipped/Failed/TimedOut/pre-feature runs;
    // percentile ignores nulls so those don't drag the median to 0.
    // Drop zero/negative readings from the median - the seeder takes minutes
    // on every preset, so a 0 means the publish path captured ElapsedMs wrong
    // (or a historical bug). Letting it through would drag the median to 0.
    ['Seeder duration (s)']             = round(percentile(iif(seeder_duration_seconds > 0, seeder_duration_seconds, real(null)), 50), 0),
    // Helpers below feed Capacity status, Headroom, Bottleneck — dropped from
    // the projection at the end so they don't show in the table.
    cpu_worst     = max(plan_CpuPercentage_max),
    mem_worst     = max(plan_MemoryPercentage_max),
    sqldtu_worst  = max(sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max),
    sqlcpu_worst  = max(sql_cpu_percent_max),
    sqllog_worst  = max(sql_log_write_percent_max),
    sqlread_worst = max(sql_physical_data_read_percent_max),
    err_worst     = max(run_error_rate)
    by Tier = infra_tier
| extend ['Capacity status'] = case(
    err_worst >= 0.01
      or cpu_worst    >= 95
      or mem_worst    >= 95
      or sqldtu_worst >= 95
      or sqlcpu_worst >= 95, 'Saturated',
    cpu_worst    >= 85
      or mem_worst    >= 85
      or sqldtu_worst >= 85
      or sqlcpu_worst >= 85, 'Stressed',
    'OK')
// bn_peak is the highest peak across ALL six resources (the four used for
// Capacity status plus log-write and physical-reads). Headroom and Bottleneck
// derive from it so the 'how much room' and 'what saturated' answers agree.
| extend bn_peak = coalesce(max_of(cpu_worst, mem_worst, sqldtu_worst, sqlcpu_worst, sqllog_worst, sqlread_worst), real(0))
| extend Headroom = round(100 - bn_peak, 0)
| extend Bottleneck = case(
    bn_peak < 50, '—',
    cpu_worst == bn_peak,     strcat('App CPU ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
    mem_worst == bn_peak,     strcat('Server memory ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
    sqldtu_worst == bn_peak,  strcat('Database load ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
    sqlcpu_worst == bn_peak,  strcat('Database CPU ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
    sqllog_worst == bn_peak,  strcat('Database log-write ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
    sqlread_worst == bn_peak, strcat('Database physical reads ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
    '—')
// Decision-first column order: verdict, then context, then supporting evidence.
| project Tier, ['Capacity status'], Headroom, Bottleneck,
          Runs, ['Requests/sec'],
          ['Server CPU avg %'], ['Server CPU peak %'],
          ['Server memory peak %'],
          ['Database load avg %'], ['Database load peak %'],
          ['Database CPU peak %'],
          ['Database physical reads peak %'],
          ['Database log-write peak %'],
          ['Error %'],
          ['Seeder duration (s)']
// Sort by tier capacity rank, not alphabetical - upgrade progression should
// read top-to-bottom (Starter -> Standard -> Pro -> Enterprise).
| extend tier_rank = case(Tier == 'Starter', 1, Tier == 'Standard', 2, Tier == 'Pro', 3, Tier == 'Enterprise', 4, 99)
| order by tier_rank asc
| project-away tier_rank
content.title: Capacity verdict per tier — verdict columns on the left, supporting resource peaks on the right. Peaks are worst-case across runs (a single saturated run flags the tier).

content.query:
// Long-form (Sampler, Tier, value) + `group: Tier` in chartSettings.
// Pivoted-wide-form bars stack by default in Workbook; the explicit group
// column renders them side-by-side. Median across all matching runs per
// (sampler, tier).
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where scenario == '{TiersScenario}' and umbraco_version == '{TiersVersion}'
| where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| extend value = case(
    '{TiersMetric}' == 'p95 (ms)', toreal(p95_ms),
    '{TiersMetric}' == 'p99 (ms)', toreal(p99_ms),
    '{TiersMetric}' == 'avg (ms)', toreal(avg_ms),
    real(null))
| where isnotnull(value)
| summarize ['{TiersMetric}'] = round(percentile(value, 50), 0) by Sampler = scenario_name, Tier = infra_tier
| order by Sampler asc, Tier asc
content.title: Median {TiersMetric} per sampler — one bar per tier. Ignore the (Sum) totals in the legend; that's the chart engine summing medians across samplers, which isn't a meaningful number — compare individual bars.
Per-sampler detail per tier — medians across all matching runs.

content.json:
## Versions
Compare Umbraco versions for one `(scenario, tier)` combination. Answers "how does v17.3.0 compare to v17.0.0 / v18.0.0 on the same hardware running the same workload?" Aggregates across every matching run in the table — the **Runs** column shows how many runs back each median: cells with 1 run are single-run snapshots; 3+ runs is statistically meaningful. When the global filter is narrowed, the pickers default to the matching scenario/tier automatically. **Cold-start runs are excluded; see the Runs tab for those.**

parameters.name: VersionsScenario
parameters.label: Scenario
parameters.query:
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where '{Scenario}' == '*' or scenario == '{Scenario}'
| where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| distinct scenario
| where isnotempty(scenario)
| order by scenario asc

parameters.name: VersionsTier
parameters.label: Tier
parameters.query:
// Show all tiers; if the global Tier filter is set, sort the matching
// tier first so showDefault picks it. Otherwise alphabetical.
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where scenario == '{VersionsScenario}'
| where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| distinct infra_tier
| where isnotempty(infra_tier)
| extend sort_key = iif(infra_tier == '{Tier}', '0', strcat('1_', infra_tier))
| order by sort_key asc
| project infra_tier

parameters.name: VersionsBaseline
parameters.label: Baseline version
parameters.query:
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where scenario == '{VersionsScenario}' and infra_tier == '{VersionsTier}'
| where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| distinct umbraco_version
| order by parse_version(umbraco_version) asc

content.query:
// Long-form output (Sampler, Version, value) and `group: Version` in
// chartSettings — pivoted-wide-form would stack the bars; long-form
// with an explicit grouping column renders side-by-side reliably.
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where scenario == '{VersionsScenario}' and infra_tier == '{VersionsTier}'
| where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| extend value = case(
    '{VersionsMetric}' == 'p95 (ms)', toreal(p95_ms),
    '{VersionsMetric}' == 'p99 (ms)', toreal(p99_ms),
    '{VersionsMetric}' == 'avg (ms)', toreal(avg_ms),
    real(null))
| where isnotnull(value)
| summarize ['{VersionsMetric}'] = round(percentile(value, 50), 0) by Sampler = scenario_name, Version = umbraco_version
| order by Sampler asc, parse_version(Version) asc
content.title: Median {VersionsMetric} per sampler — one bar per version. Ignore the (Sum) totals in the legend; that's the chart engine summing medians across samplers, which isn't a meaningful number — compare individual bars.

content.query:
// Overall version-vs-baseline delta. For each non-baseline version,
// compute median p95/p99 per sampler, take the average % delta against
// the baseline version's median, then summarize across samplers as a
// single per-version row. 'faster_p95' counts how many samplers got
// better in the candidate; 'slower_p95' the opposite.
let baseline = LoadTestSummary_CL
    | where scenario == '{VersionsScenario}' and infra_tier == '{VersionsTier}' and umbraco_version == '{VersionsBaseline}'
    | where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
    | summarize base_p95 = percentile(p95_ms, 50), base_p99 = percentile(p99_ms, 50) by scenario_name;
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where scenario == '{VersionsScenario}' and infra_tier == '{VersionsTier}' and umbraco_version != '{VersionsBaseline}'
| where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| summarize cand_p95 = percentile(p95_ms, 50), cand_p99 = percentile(p99_ms, 50), runs = count_distinct(run_id) by scenario_name, umbraco_version
| join kind=inner baseline on scenario_name
| extend p95_delta = (cand_p95 - base_p95) / base_p95 * 100,
         p99_delta = (cand_p99 - base_p99) / base_p99 * 100
| summarize
    ['Samplers']     = count(),
    runs_min         = min(runs),
    runs_max         = max(runs),
    ['Avg p95 change %']  = round(avg(p95_delta), 0),
    ['Avg p99 change %']  = round(avg(p99_delta), 0),
    ['Samplers faster'] = countif(p95_delta < 0),
    ['Samplers slower'] = countif(p95_delta > 0)
    by Version = umbraco_version
| extend ['Runs (per sampler)'] = iif(runs_min == runs_max, tostring(runs_min), strcat(runs_min, '–', runs_max))
| project Version, Samplers, ['Runs (per sampler)'], ['Avg p95 change %'], ['Avg p99 change %'], ['Samplers faster'], ['Samplers slower']
| order by Version asc
content.title: Overall — each version vs baseline {VersionsBaseline}

content.query:
// median + worst Error %: median represents typical behavior, worst surfaces
// catastrophic single-run outliers that the median would otherwise hide
// (e.g. one run at 100% error rate in a 5-run sample → median 0%, worst 100%).
LoadTestSummary_CL
| where scenario == '{VersionsScenario}' and infra_tier == '{VersionsTier}'
| where isnotempty(scenario_name) and parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
| summarize
    Runs = count(),
    ['median p95 (ms)'] = round(percentile(p95_ms, 50), 0),
    ['p95 spread (ms)'] = round(stdev(p95_ms), 0),
    ['median p99 (ms)'] = round(percentile(p99_ms, 50), 0),
    ['median Error %']    = round(percentile(error_rate, 50) * 100, 1),
    ['worst Error %']     = round(max(error_rate) * 100, 1)
    by Sampler = scenario_name, Version = umbraco_version
| order by Sampler asc, Version asc
content.title: Per-sampler stats per version

content.json:
## Compare
Pick two runs to see per-sampler + server-side changes. The dropdowns honour the global **Time range** but ignore the other global filters — each entry is one `(run × scenario × version × tier)`, so a multi-case pipeline run shows up as several picks.

parameters.name: Baseline
parameters.label: Baseline run

parameters.name: Candidate
parameters.label: Candidate run

parameters.name: RepoCompareUrl
parameters.label: Repo compare URL prefix
parameters.description: Optional URL prefix that turns baseline+candidate commit SHAs into a clickable diff. GitHub format: `https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/compare/`. AzDO format: `https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_git/<repo>/branchCompare?baseVersion=GC&targetVersion=GC&_a=files&baseVersionType=GC&targetVersionType=GC&baseVersion=`. The SHAs are appended as `<baseline>...<candidate>` (GitHub style); leave blank to disable.

content.title: Comparing
Per-sampler change
p95 per sampler — baseline vs candidate. Ignore the (Sum) totals in the legend; that's the chart engine summing p95 values across samplers, which isn't a meaningful number — compare individual bars.

content.query:
// Resource metrics live on every per-sampler row of a given run (the
// publish script duplicates them), so arg_max picks any sampler row and
// the run-level resource fields are correct.
let b_parts = split('{Baseline}', '|');
let c_parts = split('{Candidate}', '|');
let baseline = LoadTestSummary_CL
    | where run_id == tostring(b_parts[0]) and scenario == tostring(b_parts[1]) and umbraco_version == tostring(b_parts[2]) and infra_tier == tostring(b_parts[3])
    | where parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *);
let candidate = LoadTestSummary_CL
    | where run_id == tostring(c_parts[0]) and scenario == tostring(c_parts[1]) and umbraco_version == tostring(c_parts[2]) and infra_tier == tostring(c_parts[3])
    | where parse_status == 'ok' and coalesce(cold_start, false) == false
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *);
union
    (baseline | project Metric='Server CPU peak %',      Baseline=plan_CpuPercentage_max,            Candidate=toscalar(candidate | project plan_CpuPercentage_max)),
    (baseline | project Metric='Server memory peak %',   Baseline=plan_MemoryPercentage_max,         Candidate=toscalar(candidate | project plan_MemoryPercentage_max)),
    (baseline | project Metric='Database load peak %',       Baseline=sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max,   Candidate=toscalar(candidate | project sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max)),
    (baseline | project Metric='Database CPU peak %',       Baseline=sql_cpu_percent_max,               Candidate=toscalar(candidate | project sql_cpu_percent_max)),
    (baseline | project Metric='Database log-write peak %',     Baseline=sql_log_write_percent_max,         Candidate=toscalar(candidate | project sql_log_write_percent_max)),
    (baseline | project Metric='Database physical reads peak %', Baseline=sql_physical_data_read_percent_max, Candidate=toscalar(candidate | project sql_physical_data_read_percent_max)),
    (baseline | project Metric='Server HTTP 4xx peak',          Baseline=app_Http4xx_max,                   Candidate=toscalar(candidate | project app_Http4xx_max)),
    (baseline | project Metric='Server HTTP 5xx peak',          Baseline=app_Http5xx_max,                   Candidate=toscalar(candidate | project app_Http5xx_max))
| extend Baseline = round(Baseline, 1), Candidate = round(Candidate, 1)
| extend ['change %'] = iif(Baseline == 0 or isnull(Baseline) or isnull(Candidate), real(null), round((Candidate - Baseline) / Baseline * 100.0, 0)),
         Note = case(
             isnull(Baseline) and isnull(Candidate), 'no data either side',
             isnull(Baseline),                       'no baseline data',
             isnull(Candidate),                      'no candidate data',
             Baseline == 0 and Candidate == 0,       'both zero',
             Baseline == 0,                          'baseline zero',
             '')
content.title: Server-side change

content.json:
## Runs
All runs matching the global filter. To inspect a specific run's per-sampler detail, pick it from the **Drill into run #** dropdown below — the detail panel only renders when one is selected. The two **URL prefix** fields are optional: set them once to turn Run # → AzDO build links and Commit short-SHAs → repo commit links in the table.

parameters.name: DrillRun
parameters.label: Drill into run #

parameters.name: AzdoOrgUrl
parameters.label: AzDO build URL prefix (ends in ?buildId=)
parameters.description: Optional URL prefix — NOT a run number. Paste your pipeline's full result URL up to and including `?buildId=`, e.g. `https://dev.azure.com/myorg/myproject/_build/results?buildId=`. The run number from each row is appended automatically, turning Run # cells in the table below into clickable links. Leave blank to disable.

parameters.name: RepoCommitUrl
parameters.label: Repo commit URL prefix
parameters.description: Optional URL prefix that turns the Commit short-SHA into a clickable link. GitHub format: `https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/commit/`. AzDO format: `https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_git/<repo>/commit/`. The commit SHA is appended automatically. Leave blank to disable.

content.query:
// Group by (run_id × scenario × version × tier) so a pipeline run that
// covered multiple cases shows one row per case. parse_status filter
// excludes the regression_check rows from the load-test summary, then we
// leftouter-join them back to surface the regression verdict per case.
let runs = LoadTestSummary_CL
    | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
    | where '{Scenario}' == '*' or scenario == '{Scenario}'
    | where '{Version}' == '*' or umbraco_version == '{Version}'
    | where '{Tier}' == '*' or infra_tier == '{Tier}'
    | where parse_status in ('ok', 'no_metrics', 'no_results_dir')
    | extend run_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', tostring(run_id))), scenario_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', scenario)), version_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', umbraco_version)), tier_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', infra_tier))
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by run_key, scenario_key, version_key, tier_key;
let regression = LoadTestSummary_CL
    | where parse_status == 'regression_check'
    | extend run_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', tostring(run_id))), scenario_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', scenario)), version_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', umbraco_version)), tier_key = tolower(trim(@'\s+', infra_tier))
    | summarize regression_status = take_any(regression_status), regressed_count = take_any(regressed_count), reg_ts = max(TimeGenerated) by run_key, scenario_key, version_key, tier_key;
runs
| join kind=leftouter regression on run_key, scenario_key, version_key, tier_key
| extend ['Build URL'] = iif(strlen('{AzdoOrgUrl}') > 0, strcat('{AzdoOrgUrl}', run_id), '')
| extend bn_peak = coalesce(max_of(plan_CpuPercentage_max, plan_MemoryPercentage_max, sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max, sql_cpu_percent_max, sql_log_write_percent_max, sql_physical_data_read_percent_max), real(0))
// Decision-first column order: row identifier, then verdict triple
// (Regression / Bottleneck / Regressed #), then reference / metadata columns.
| project Started=TimeGenerated,
          Scenario=scenario,
          Version=umbraco_version,
          Tier=infra_tier,
          ['Cold start']=coalesce(cold_start, false),
          Regression=case(
              regression_status == 'regress',      'regression detected',
              regression_status == 'pass',         'no regression',
              regression_status == 'insufficient', 'not enough history',
              isnotempty(regression_status),       regression_status,
              TimeGenerated > ago(15min),          'checking',
              'not run'),
          Bottleneck=case(
              bn_peak < 50, '—',
              plan_CpuPercentage_max == bn_peak, strcat('App CPU ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              plan_MemoryPercentage_max == bn_peak, strcat('Server memory ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              sql_dtu_consumption_percent_max == bn_peak, strcat('Database load ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              sql_cpu_percent_max == bn_peak, strcat('Database CPU ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              sql_log_write_percent_max == bn_peak, strcat('Database log-write ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              sql_physical_data_read_percent_max == bn_peak, strcat('Database physical reads ', round(bn_peak, 0), '%'),
              '—'),
          ['Regressed #']=coalesce(regressed_count, 0),
          ['Run #']=run_id,
          ['Build URL']=['Build URL'],
          Commit=substring(column_ifexists("commit", ""), 0, 8),
          ['Parse status']=parse_status,
          ['Commit URL'] = iif(strlen('{RepoCommitUrl}') > 0 and strlen(column_ifexists("commit", "")) > 0, strcat('{RepoCommitUrl}', column_ifexists("commit", "")), '')
| order by Started desc
content.title: Runs
Regression breakdown for selected run
Per-sampler detail for selected run
Per-minute resource pressure (% metrics) — App / SQL CPU, DTU, log-write, physical reads.
Per-minute HTTP error counts — 4xx (client errors) + 5xx (server errors). Auto-scaled Y-axis.

content.json:
## Client measurements
Client-side perceived latency in the Umbraco backoffice. All numbers are averages across runs.

- **Summary table** — avg median / p75 / p95 / stddev (+ run count) by metric × tier × version
- **Cold vs cached** — avg cold vs cached load times + cache savings %
- **Browser timing** — avg TTFB / DCL / load / LCP marks per metric × tier
- **Segment table** — avg time-to-first-edit breakdown: login / navigate / editor-ready / keystroke

content.query: ClientMeasurement_CL | where metric == "time_to_first_edit" | summarize Runs=dcount(run_id), total_ms=round(avg(median_ms),1), login_ms=round(avg(seg_login_ms),1), navigate_ms=round(avg(seg_navigate_ms),1), editor_ready_ms=round(avg(seg_editor_ready_ms),1), keystroke_ms=round(avg(seg_keystroke_ms),1) by infra_tier, umbraco_version | order by infra_tier asc
content.title: Time-to-first-edit segments (avg ms)
Time-to-first-edit (avg total ms) — one bar per tier, grouped by version (lower = better)

content.query: ClientMeasurement_CL | where isnotempty(metric) | summarize Runs=count(), median_ms=round(avg(median_ms),1), p75_ms=round(avg(p75_ms),1), p95_ms=round(avg(p95_ms),1), stddev_ms=round(avg(stddev_ms),1) by metric, infra_tier, umbraco_version | extend _ord = case(metric == "cold_dashboard_load",1, metric == "cached_dashboard_load",2, metric == "cold_homenode_load",3, metric == "cached_homenode_load",4, metric == "time_to_first_edit",5, 9) | order by infra_tier asc, _ord asc | project-away _ord
content.title: Summary by metric × tier × version (avg)

content.query: ClientMeasurement_CL | where metric in ("cold_dashboard_load","cached_dashboard_load","cold_homenode_load","cached_homenode_load") | extend page = iff(metric has "dashboard", "Welcome dashboard", "Homepage node") | summarize Runs=dcount(run_id), cold_ms=round(avgif(median_ms, metric startswith "cold"),1), cached_ms=round(avgif(median_ms, metric startswith "cached"),1) by page, infra_tier, umbraco_version | extend cache_savings_pct = round(100.0 * (cold_ms - cached_ms) / cold_ms, 1) | order by infra_tier asc, page asc
content.title: Cold vs cached load (avg median ms) + cache savings

content.query: ClientMeasurement_CL | where metric in ("cold_dashboard_load","cached_dashboard_load","cold_homenode_load","cached_homenode_load") | summarize ttfb_ms=round(avg(ttfb_ms),1), dcl_ms=round(avg(dcl_ms),1), load_ms=round(avg(load_ms),1), lcp_ms=round(avg(lcp_ms),1) by metric, infra_tier | extend _ord = case(metric == "cold_dashboard_load",1, metric == "cached_dashboard_load",2, metric == "cold_homenode_load",3, metric == "cached_homenode_load",4, 9) | order by infra_tier asc, _ord asc | project-away _ord
content.title: Browser timing marks (avg ms; lcp is usually null in the headless backoffice SPA)

content.json:
**Browser timing marks** — standard Web Performance API timings, measured from navigation start (lower = better):
- **TTFB** (Time To First Byte) — the first response byte arrives. Reflects server + network latency, before any rendering.
- **DCL** (DOMContentLoaded) — HTML parsed and the DOM built (images/CSS not yet awaited). The page structure is ready.
- **load** — every resource (JS, CSS, images, fonts) has finished loading. Full-load time.
- **LCP** (Largest Contentful Paint) — the largest content element is painted; closest to "the page appeared". Often **null** here, because the headless backoffice SPA has no classic LCP element.

## Glossary

### Entities
- **Run** — one pipeline build. Identified by `Run #` (the AzDO build ID).
- **Case** — one (scenario × version × tier) slice. A multi-case pipeline run produces several rows per `Run #`.
- **Scenario** — the workload YAML under `loadtests/scenarios/` (e.g. `BackofficeOnly`).
- **Sampler** — one Locust task inside a scenario (an individual endpoint or operation). Shown as `Sampler` in tables (underlying column: `scenario_name`).
- **Tier** — the Azure App Service + SQL Database pairing the case ran on (e.g. Starter, Standard, Premium).

### Metrics
- **p95 / p99** — 95th / 99th percentile of per-request latency in milliseconds. *5 in 100 / 1 in 100* requests were slower than this.
- **Max** — the single slowest request observed for that sampler during the run. One observation, not an aggregate. Useful for spotting outliers; noisy run-to-run.
- **Requests/sec** — throughput the case sustained.
- **Error %** — percentage of requests that failed.
- **Server CPU avg / peak %** — average and peak Azure App Service Plan CPU during the run.
- **Database load avg / peak %** — average and peak Azure SQL Database load (Azure's bundled CPU + IO measure, internally called DTU).
- **Database CPU peak %** — peak Azure SQL Database CPU during the run (the CPU portion only, distinct from `Database load` which bundles CPU + IO).
- **Database physical reads peak %** — peak fraction of database reads that hit disk instead of memory cache. Rises *before* DTU saturates — a leading indicator that SQL is memory-constrained.
- **Database log-write peak %** — peak fraction of the database's transaction-log throughput budget consumed during the run. Surfaces write-heavy bottlenecks (inserts/updates/deletes); pairs with `Database CPU peak %` to separate write pressure from read/compute pressure.
- **Server HTTP 4xx peak / Server HTTP 5xx peak** — peak count of client errors (4xx — auth failures, validation, missing endpoints) and server errors (5xx — crashes, unhandled exceptions) seen during the run.
- **spread** — one standard deviation across the runs that produced the median. Rough indicator of variability; latency is skewed so treat as indicative, not symmetric.
- **change %** — percentage difference vs. the chosen baseline. *Negative* = candidate is faster than baseline, *positive* = slower.

### Verdicts
- **Capacity status** — verdict on a run's infrastructure: *Saturated* (any resource ≥ 95% or error rate ≥ 1%), *Stressed* (any resource ≥ 85%), or *OK*.
- **Headroom** — `100 − highest peak %` across all monitored resources. The buffer before the most-saturated resource hits ceiling; higher = more room to grow.
- **Bottleneck** — names the hottest resource and its peak (e.g. `Database load 92%`). Tells you *what* saturated. `—` means everything was below 50%.
- **Stability** — how consistent the metric was across runs in this cell. *stable* (CV < 10%), *moderate* (10–25%), *noisy* (≥ 25%), *few runs* (< 5). Noisy cells need wider regression thresholds — a 10% regression in a 30%-noise cell is indistinguishable from run-to-run variance.
- **Regression** — verdict from `scripts/check-regression.ps1` comparing this run's p95/p99/error against the cell's baseline median: *regression detected*, *no regression*, *not enough history*, *checking*, *not run*.
- **Cold start** — `true` if the run skipped warmup (queue parameter `skipWarmup: true`). Cold-start runs are excluded from Trends/Tiers/Versions by default; visible on Runs.

### Layout
The global filter scopes **Trends**, **Compare**, and **Runs**. The **Tiers** and **Versions** tabs have their own pickers but inherit the global filter when one is set.
